hero.subtitle: Single-window national Computer Based Test (CBT) conducted by NTA for undergraduate admissions across Central Universities, State Universities, Deemed Universities, Other Government Institutions, and Private Universities.

key_facts.label: Max Subject Choice
key_facts.value: Up to 5 Subjects | 50 Compulsory MCQs / Paper

syllabus.session_label: CUET (UG) Official Subject-Wise Syllabi (37 Subjects — Appendix II)
syllabus.overview: NTA prescribes 37 subjects under Appendix II of the CUET (UG) Information Bulletin: 13 Languages (Codes 101–113), 23 Domain-Specific Subjects (Codes 301–326), and 1 General Aptitude Test (Code 501). Every subject has a dedicated official syllabus PDF hosted on cuet.nta.nic.in.

exam_pattern.overview: CUET (UG) is conducted in Computer Based Test (CBT) mode across multiple shifts. Candidates can opt for up to 5 subjects/languages. Each subject paper consists of 50 compulsory Multiple Choice Questions to be attempted in 60 minutes.

papers.duration: 60 Minutes per paper (+20 mins/hr compensatory time for eligible PwD/PwBD)

papers.section: Section II — Domain-Specific Subjects (23 Subjects: Codes 301–326)
papers.questions: 50 Compulsory MCQs per chosen domain subject
papers.duration: 60 Minutes per paper (+20 mins/hr compensatory time for eligible PwD/PwBD)

papers.questions: 50 Compulsory MCQs (GK, Current Affairs, General Mental Ability, Numerical Ability, Quantitative Reasoning, Logical & Analytical Reasoning)
papers.duration: 60 Minutes (+20 mins/hr compensatory time for eligible PwD/PwBD)

marking_scheme.marks: +5 Marks to those who marked any correct option; +5 Marks to all appeared candidates if dropped

mediums: Urdu (13 Languages; Sanskrit 325 is not translated into other languages)
exam_pattern.normalization: For multi-shift papers, raw marks obtained by candidates in different shifts are normalized into Percentile Scores (NTA Scores) per Appendix VI of the Information Bulletin. CUET (UG) NTA Scores are valid for admission to the respective academic year only.

eligibility.age_limit: For appearing in CUET (UG), there is NO age limit set by NTA. However, candidates must satisfy the age criteria (if any) of the specific University / Institution / Organization to which they seek admission.
eligibility.qualifying_exam: Candidates who have passed the Class 12 / equivalent examination or are appearing in Class 12 in the current year are eligible to appear in CUET (UG), irrespective of age.
eligibility.university_mapping_rule: Merely appearing in CUET (UG) does not confer any right to admission. Subject combinations, minimum Class 12 percentage, and programme-specific eligibility vary by each Central/State/Deemed/Private University — candidates must verify course mapping on the respective university's website.
